subject: Clarify billing on cached responses for session-affinity and conversational state
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acmecorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+billing@acmecorp.com
Date: 2028-04-07T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cached responses — charging boundaries?

Hi Stephanie,

Quick question as we prep our SOW and cost model: when Redwood returns a cached response (e.g., a prefix/prompt-state cache hit inside an active session), does Acme get billed for the tokens in that cached output, or only for the tokens that the model actually executed? We have a couple of variations that are tripping up our finance team: 

1) Exact prefix hit: user input matches a cached prefix and Redwood returns stored output without invoking the model.
2) Partial reuse: a cached KV-state is used but the runtime needs to generate an additional 8 tokens to stitch the response.
3) Cross-session re-use: a user hits an identical prompt that was generated for a different session — same output, different session id.

Can you provide a short written definition we can put in procurement (e.g., what counts as a billable token vs. a cache-returned token) plus 1–2 numerical examples so our FP&A can run scenarios?

Also: we will likely ask for a short addendum in the contract if hits are free — to explicitly call out session-affinity semantics and any limits. Can Redwood share a suggested clause or a template addendum and the relevant ratecard SKU mapping?

Thanks — Emily
Emily Ross
Head of Product Operations, AcmeCorp

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cached responses — charging boundaries?

Hi Emily — great question, and glad you flagged the procurement ask. Below is the short definition we use internally and the examples your FP&A team can model against. I attached a short pricing matrix and our current hosted ratecard for reference.

Short definition (plain language):
- Billable tokens = any token for which Redwood executed model compute during the request.
- Cache-returned tokens = tokens returned directly from the prefix/prompt-state cache where no model forward pass was executed; these are not billed as model tokens.
- Partial-execution case = if the runtime rehydrates a cached KV/state and then executes the model to produce additional tokens, Redwood bills only for the tokens produced by the model execution, not for the cached portion that was returned intact.
- Cross-session identical-output: cache hits are evaluated by content-addressing + tenant policy; if the platform returns the exact cached bytes without invoking the model, those tokens are not billed even across sessions (subject to contract-level restrictions and customer opt-in on cross-session cache sharing).

Numeric examples (simple):
- Example A (exact prefix hit): 0 model tokens executed, 250 tokens returned from cache -> billed model tokens = 0.
- Example B (partial reuse): cached 200-token prefix reused, runtime generates 8 new tokens -> billed model tokens = 8.
- Example C (cross-session): identical cached reply reused across sessions, no model executed -> billed model tokens = 0 (requires cross-session cache sharing enabled in account).

Notes and caveats:
- Short-lived cache TTLs and eviction can cause otherwise-expected hits to miss; misses will result in normal model billing.
- Some enterprise customers opt into a "warm-cache" prefetching service (charged as prefetch compute) — we can map that to a separate SKU if you want to avoid surprises in month 1.
- Auditing: we produce per-request traces and token-level billing records in the Console so you can reconcile line-items on invoices.

We attached: redwood-cache-pricing-matrix.xlsx (maps behaviors to SKUs) and redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf. I'm happy to draft a short contract addendum; Vivek and Marissa are looped for pricing and legal/contract ops. 

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through your FP&A scenarios?

Best,
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Cached responses — charging boundaries?

Looping legal / pricing ops note: we should offer a clean addendum that states the billing logic above and explicitly calls out cross-session sharing as an opt-in feature. For ACME specifically I'm supportive of a migration credit for the first 60 days (e.g., up to $10k) if they enable cross-session caching — reduces friction for them and is low cost for us if they drive traffic. Marissa can you check with contracts and produce a 1-paragraph clause we can add to the SOW?

— Vivek

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acmecorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+billing@acmecorp.com
Date: 2028-04-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cached responses — charging boundaries?

Thanks, Stephanie — that is very helpful and much clearer than our initial assumptions. The numeric examples are exactly what FP&A asked for.

We'd like the addendum to explicitly call out: cross-session cache sharing (opt-in), TTL/eviction expectations, and the prefetch SKU option. If you can draft wording we can push through procurement. We can also accept a one-time migration credit; will surface to finance.

Can you send the DocuSign template for the addendum and a final XLS with the SKU mapping (so we can line-item to our budget)? Once we have that we'll queue it with our legal and procurement team — target is to have it signed during contract signature next week.
